curation.lead:
The Elizabeth Ross Johnson Trust is a revocable trust established by Elizabeth Ross Johnson (1924–2017), known as "Libet" Johnson, the granddaughter of Johnson & Johnson founder Robert Wood Johnson I. Property records from Deutsche Bank due diligence documents (EFTA01296720) place both Johnson and Jeffrey Epstein as co-owners of 375 Mill Creek Circle in Vail, Colorado — a property appraised at $19,280,153 — with both parties listing Epstein's business office at 457 Madison Avenue, New York, NY, as their shared address. [Finding #582] LittleSis records (entity 462224; relationship 2027530) confirm Epstein held an ownership relationship with the trust and managed Johnson's money as a professional advisor. [Finding #1552]

The trust was formally restructured on May 13, 1998, as the "Elizabeth Ross Johnson Amended and Restated Revocable Trust Indenture," naming Christopher Wold Johnson as co-trustee alongside Johnson. [Finding #644] Three months later, on August 26, 1998, an Eagle County, Colorado deed (Document Number 670194) executed an INTRAFAMILY TRANSFER AND DISSOLUTION removing Epstein from the Vail property title, handled by Stewart Title. [Finding #584] The two transactions — trust restructuring in May and Epstein's removal from the deed in August — occurred within the same calendar year. [Finding #645] After the restructuring, Johnson's property transactions were routed through legal counsel at Baer Marks and Upham LLP (805 Third Avenue) and later Kramer Levin Naftalis, rather than through Epstein's 457 Madison Avenue operations. [Finding #1552]

ACRIS records document at least 13 New York City real estate transactions executed by the trust between 2004 and 2013, comprising sales of multiple units at 1 Central Park West totaling over $63 million, a $2 million acquisition from Keller Enterprises LLC, and a $20 million mortgage from Morgan Stanley Private Bank, establishing total documented NYC real estate activity exceeding $65 million. [Finding #644] The trust was also administered in part through TAG Associates Ltd at 75 Rockefeller Plaza. [Finding #1552] FedEx shipping records show Epstein dispatching packages on behalf of Elizabeth Ross Johnson to Harvard University's History of Science department during the period of the trust relationship. [Finding #1554]
curation.system_role: The Elizabeth Ross Johnson Trust represents one of Epstein's earliest documented high-net-worth client relationships — predating the fully documented Wexner engagement — in which a Johnson & Johnson heiress with a real estate portfolio exceeding $65 million used Epstein's business address as her own and co-held property with him under an intrafamily deed classification, before restructuring the trust under family co-trusteeship in 1998 and transitioning property management to independent legal counsel.

sections.title: Property Co-Ownership and Shared Business Address
sections.content:
The earliest documented evidence of the Epstein-Johnson financial relationship is a deed record from Eagle County, Colorado, retrieved through Deutsche Bank due diligence files (EFTA01296720). The record shows Elizabeth Ross Johnson as both seller and co-buyer with Jeffrey E. Epstein of 375 Mill Creek Circle, Vail, CO 81657, with a total assessed market value of $19,280,153 (land: $1,626,790; improvements: $17,653,363). Both Johnson and Epstein listed 457 Madison Avenue, New York, NY 10022 as their address on the deed — the same address used by J. Epstein & Co., DKIP LLC, and multiple other Epstein-controlled entities. [Finding #582] The practical effect was that Johnson's real estate affairs were processed through Epstein's business infrastructure. [Finding #585]

The legal classification of the subsequent transfer is notable. On August 26, 1998 (recorded September 21, 1998), the co-ownership was dissolved via a deed typed as INTRAFAMILY TRANSFER AND DISSOLUTION (Document Number 670194), with Stewart Title as the title company. [Finding #584] The intrafamily designation indicates the parties characterized their relationship as familially proximate for purposes of the transfer. The Vail property was subsequently sold for a reported $24 million. [Finding #584] The account of the sale to French buyers who reportedly never visited the property has not been independently verified in primary records as of this writing.

sections.title: Trust Restructuring and Transition to Independent Counsel
sections.content:
The Elizabeth Ross Johnson Amended and Restated Revocable Trust Indenture was executed on May 13, 1998, with Christopher Wold Johnson serving as co-trustee. [Finding #644] Three months later, the INTRAFAMILY TRANSFER AND DISSOLUTION deed removed Epstein from the Vail property on August 26, 1998. The contemporaneous timing of the trust restructuring and the deed dissolution — occurring within the same year, three months apart — is documented in the record; whether one transaction caused the other is an inference, not confirmed by the available documents. [Finding #645]

Following the 1998 restructuring, the trust's legal representation shifted to Baer Marks and Upham LLP at 805 Third Avenue, and later to Kramer Levin Naftalis. Property transactions after 1998 used the trust's own address at 1 Central Park West, New York, NY 10023, rather than Epstein's 457 Madison Avenue business address. [Finding #1552] The trust was also administered in part through TAG Associates Ltd at 75 Rockefeller Plaza. [Finding #1552] Whether Epstein retained any advisory role after the 1998 restructuring is not established by available primary sources.

sections.title: New York City Real Estate Portfolio
sections.content:
ACRIS records document at least 13 transactions executed by the Elizabeth Ross Johnson Trust at two Manhattan addresses between 2001 and 2013. At 1 Central Park West (Block 1113), the trust sold five residential units: Lot 1537 for $13 million (August 2005) to Sarah Merritt Eastman and Kevin Pinto [ACRIS:2005090101295001]; Lot 1539 for $6.9 million (March 2006) to Andrew Rosen [ACRIS:2006032700486001]; Lot 1541 for $18.5 million (January 2007) to North-51 LLC [ACRIS:2007011600137001]; Lot 1532 for $21.85 million (June 2013) to Unit 48A CPW LLC [ACRIS:2013070900801001]; and Lot 1438 for $3.475 million (October 2013) to Placid Sadie LLC [ACRIS:2013102500557001]. The trust also purchased Lot 1438 for $2 million (November 2004) from Keller Enterprises LLC, and acquired Lot 1540 (2001) from Wang Family Holdings LLC. [Finding #644]

A separate $20 million mortgage from Morgan Stanley Private Bank (2012) is associated with a Queens property. The trust also transferred property at 16 East 69th Street as grantor in 2012. [Finding #1554] Aggregate documented NYC real estate activity for the trust exceeded $65 million. [Finding #644] During the trust relationship, FedEx records show Epstein dispatching packages from Elizabeth Ross Johnson addressed to Harvard University's History of Science department at Oxford Street, Cambridge, MA. [Finding #1554]

sections.title: Network Connections: Family, Epstein Infrastructure, and Financial Relationships
sections.content:
LittleSis documents four primary relationships for Johnson. Her professional relationship with Jeffrey Epstein (LittleSis relationship 2027530) is characterized as Epstein managing her money. Her ownership relationship with the trust (LittleSis relationship 2040592) is separately documented. A familial relationship connects her to Woody Johnson (LittleSis relationship 1501668) — Robert Wood Johnson IV, owner of the New York Jets and U.S. Ambassador to the United Kingdom under Trump. A social relationship with hairstylist Frederic Fekkai (LittleSis relationship 2037601) is documented as ending around 2001; a 2003 New York Post article (EFTA01334074) references a wealthy girlfriend providing Fekkai a Gulfstream jet. [Finding #1556]

According to a source quoted in the LittleSis record, Epstein's access to Johnson's wealth came through Les Wexner: "Wexner gave him legitimacy as a money manager for the wealthy, and he began handling the portfolio of Elizabeth Ross Johnson." [Finding #1556] The trust also carries database connections — through Epstein's broader entity network — to Gratitude America Ltd (Epstein's USVI private foundation), the International Peace Institute, and the Deutsche Bank compliance infrastructure that processed Johnson property records as part of Epstein due diligence. These connections flow through the Epstein entity network rather than directly from the trust itself. [Findings #1728, #1744]

open_questions: What was the duration of Epstein's active management of Johnson's finances? The deed co-ownership is documented as early as the early 1990s (the property was assessed at 1990s values) and the trust dissolution occurred in 1998, but the start date of Epstein's advisory role has not been established from primary sources.

Did Epstein retain any role — formal or informal — in managing Johnson's finances after the 1998 trust restructuring and his removal from the Vail deed? The shift to independent legal counsel (Baer Marks and Upham LLP, Kramer Levin Naftalis) is documented, but no primary source confirms complete separation.

What was the mechanism by which Epstein became co-owner of a $19.28 million Vail property alongside Johnson, and what consideration, if any, did Epstein provide? The deed records show both parties as buyers at 457 Madison Avenue, but the terms of any financial arrangement between them are not in available documents.

The FedEx records showing Epstein shipping packages from Johnson to Harvard's History of Science department — what was the content, and does it connect to Epstein's documented pattern of cultivating academic relationships through wealthy client networks?

What is the relationship between Johnson's trust and the broader TAG Associates Ltd management infrastructure at 75 Rockefeller Plaza? TAG Associates appears in the trust's administrative records; whether it provided portfolio management services consistent with the scale of the documented real estate holdings (over $65 million in NYC transactions alone) has not been independently verified.
